subject: Private stack: CI safety gates and dependency freeze for IaC modules
messages:
From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@acme-retail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@acme-retail.com
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private stack kickoff - initial IaC questions

Thanks Vanessa — quick follow-up from the infra team call this morning. Before we proceed with the on-prem bundle, can you confirm the following so we can complete our security review checklist?

1) Will Redwood's CI pipelines produce signed module artifacts that we can verify in our air-gapped environment?
2) Who owns the Terraform module semantic versioning policy for the private stack (patch vs minor vs major)?
3) Any known transitive dependency on public registries at apply time (e.g., remote providers, helm charts pulled from helm.pkg)?

We attached our initial dependency matrix and a crude zone map. Once we have these answers, security will schedule a short follow-up.

— Rajesh
Infra Lead, Acme Retail
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private stack kickoff - initial IaC questions

Rajesh — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and I'll add a short doc to Drive tonight: ci-safety-gates.md

1) Signed artifacts: yes. Our CI publishes SHA256 manifests and GPG signatures for module tarballs and helm charts. For private deployments we can mirror signed artifacts to your air-gap staging bucket; the installer supports local artifact paths.

2) Module versioning: Redwood owns the module repo but we follow semantic versioning. For private stacks we recommend pinning at minor (e.g., 1.3.x) in module consumers and we support controlled patch roll-forwards via our CD job. If Acme needs a stricter policy we can adopt a freeze window.

3) Transitive pulls: by default some Helm charts reference public registries. We have a 'static bundle' mode that vendorizes all charts and providers at build time; the bundle contains the provider plugins and chart tgzs so no external network calls at apply.

Action items I suggest:
- Redwood to deliver a signed artifact bundle + verification script (we will send by Thu).
- Acme to confirm preferred pinning policy (freeze until security sign-off or rolling patches allowed).
- Schedule 30m sandbox run with mirrored artifacts in your staging lab next week.

Attaching the dependency matrix and a draft of our CI safety gates (see attachments).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Feb 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private stack kickoff - initial IaC questions

On Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 11:04 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rajesh — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and I'll add a short doc to Drive tonight: ci-safety-gates.md

Adding some implementation specifics from the infra/runtime team so Acme's engineers can validate locally:

- Artifact signing: we use cosign for container artifacts and GPG for terraform module tarballs. Verification scripts are included in the bundle under /scripts/verify-artifacts.sh and support both keyserver and local public-key files.
- Provider plugins: we vendor provider binaries and set TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR to the local bundle path before terraform init; the installer sets TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR for the execution environment.
- Helm charts: charts are packaged into tgz and checksums are included in the manifest. Helm pulls are disabled if BUNDLE_MODE=static.
- CI gates: proposed checks in pipeline (pre-apply):
  * signature verification pass
  * dependency matrix drift <= 0 (i.e., no unexpected external pulls)
  * terraform fmt + validate + lint (tflint/basic rules)
  * plan approval only after policy checks (opa/gatekeeper rules)

If Acme wants, we can add a lightweight SBOM for module artifacts. I'll volunteer to pair with your SRE to run a mirrored apply in your staging lab.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@acme-retail.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Megan Liu <megan@edgeops.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private stack: CI safety gates and dependency freeze for IaC modules

Rajesh / Acme team — thanks for continuing the review and for the lab time last week. Quick executive confirmation from Redwood:

- We will provide the signed bundle and verification scripts by EOD Friday (Feb 13).
- Redwood recommends a short dependency freeze for initial cutover: block minor upgrades for 2 weeks post-deploy, allow security patches only via a gated patch pipeline.
- We agree that the CI safety gates listed by Dev should be enforced in your staging CD; Redwood will add an OPA policy example and a tflint ruleset to the shared Drive.

Next steps:
1) Vanessa to upload the signed bundle and ci-safety-gates.md link (vanessa: pls include verify-artifacts.sh sample).
2) Rajesh to confirm freeze window (2 weeks or alternate) and provide SRE contact for sandbox schedule.
3) Markus and Grace will be on standby for the first mirrored apply and will monitor for any networking host/route issues.

If Acme agrees, we'll also include a small rollback playbook (Ansible snippet) that your ops team can run offline to revert the installer.

— Irene Choi
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
